title: Quantifying the Persona Effect in LLM Simulations

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating zero-shot LLM predictions by integrating race and ethnicity variables into persona prompts to measure how well the model simulates race-specific annotator variance using R-squared, Cohen's Kappa, and Mean Absolute Error.
Prepending gender identity and transgender status to LLM prompts to assess the model's capacity to replicate gender-based differences in human annotations on subjective NLP tasks.

Incorporating political leaning and affiliation into persona descriptions to measure the model's ability to predict political survey responses (ANES) and subjective task annotations aligned with specific political ideologies.
Adding age range variables to persona prompts to evaluate if the model can accurately simulate age-related perspectives and variances in human labeling behavior.
Appending variables regarding the importance of religion in the annotator's life to the prompt to test the model's simulation of religion-based perspectives.
Using LGBTQ+ status in persona descriptions to measure the LLM's capability to capture the specific annotation patterns and perspectives of this demographic group.
Including education level, employment status, and occupation in the persona prompts to calculate the variance these socioeconomic factors explain in the model's simulated annotations.
Integrating country of birth, country of residence, and nationality into persona variables to evaluate the model's alignment with geographically and culturally diverse human annotators.
